text:
sora: hey all, new hire here. trying to run `kubectl get pods -n default` but get: "error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)". I logged into the SSO yesterday. kubectl context shows `redwood-dev` and user `sora@redwood` so i'm confused. any quick debugging steps?

kevin: welcome! first guess is your OIDC token expired. which auth exec plugin does your kubeconfig use? `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].user.exec.command}'` should show `aws-iam-authenticator` or `rdw-sso` or similar.

sora: output is `rdw-sso`. how do i refresh?

kevin: try `rdw-sso login` (our wrapper) or run `kubectl login` if you have the login shim. you can also check timestamp: `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].user.exec.env[?(@.name=="TOKEN_EXPIRY")].value}'` to see expiry.

sora: i ran `rdw-sso login` and it opened a browser for SSO. after finishing i still get Unauthorized.

devex-bot: Onboarding K8s guide: https://docs.internal/redwood/onboarding/k8s-auth. Tip: if you used the browser SSO from a different machine the token won't apply locally; make sure you complete the login flow on this terminal.

kevin: another possibility: we issue short-lived tokens that map to a temporary rolebinding. check `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n default` to confirm. if that returns no, the RBAC entry might not be created yet.

sora: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n default` -> no. i did submit an access request in the portal (ONB-520) but it's pending review.

infra-oncall: i can fast-track ephemeral dev view for new hires. what's the user string? `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.users[0].name}'`

sora: `sora@redwood`

infra-oncall: okay creating RoleBinding `rb-onboard-sora` in namespace `team-sora` with role `view` for 48h. will attach ticket ONB-520.

auth-bot: Auth system note: created rolebinding rb-onboard-sora (user: sora@redwood) expires in 48h. Audit ID: A-98765. Reminder will be posted 24h before expiry.

kevin: after infra-oncall applies it, try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-sora` then `kubectl get pods -n team-sora`. Also double-check which kubeconfig is active: `echo $KUBECONFIG` or `kubectl config view --minify --raw` to confirm it's using the portal one.

sora: tried `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-sora` -> yes now. `kubectl get pods -n team-sora` shows two pods. thanks!

kevin: one more safety: install `kubectx` and `kubens` and add this alias to your shellrc: `alias kdev='KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/contexts/dev.yaml kubectl --context=redwood-dev-sora'` so you don't accidentally hit prod. we also recommend `kubectl version --client` to ensure your client is recent; older clients sometimes fail with newer auth plugins.

sora: client is v1.26.0. i'll add the alias. thanks everyone, closing this thread :)
